page.title: Keys & packs
page.description: Packs add tools. Add the keys they need, and turn them on or off.
page.noMatchHint: Clear the search to see every pack.
page.chooseHint: Pick a pack from the list to see what it may do, its keys and its tools.

consent.title: Turn on {name}?
consent.description: This pack was not shipped with plughive. Check what it may do before you turn it on.
consent.errorChanged: The pack's files changed since this review was loaded. Review the updated permissions below.
consent.errorConsentRequired: The daemon needs a fresh review before turning this pack on.
consent.broadAccessTitle: This pack asks for broad access
consent.broadAccessBody: It can run programs or reach any website. Only turn it on if you trust where it came from.
consent.fullRightsTitle: Its code runs with your full rights
consent.fullRightsBody: Turning this pack on lets its code run on this computer with your full rights: it can do anything you can. The lines below describe what plughive mediates for it, not a sandbox.
consent.mayNothing: Nothing beyond working on what you pass it.
consent.keysHint: The pack only sees the keys you allow here.

detail.turnedOffUndo: {name} turned off. Its tools are gone from every profile.
detail.reviewBody: The pack changed or asks for new access. Review it to turn it on again.
detail.servicesHintBefore: Jobs your agent asks for through the shared tools, which this pack can do. Choose which service goes first on
detail.noToolsShared: No tools of its own: agents use it through the shared tools for its services.
detail.noTools: This pack has no tools right now.
detail.noToolsOff: Turn the pack on to load its tools.

secret.envNote: This key comes from an environment variable. A key saved here takes its place.
secret.removeBody: Tools that need this key stop working until you set it again. The stored value is deleted and cannot be shown again.

storage.secretsFileFallback: secrets.json in the plughive data folder

words.keychain: Keys are saved in the macOS Keychain on this computer.
words.keychainService: Keys are saved in the macOS Keychain on this computer, under the service name {service}.
words.keyring: Keys are saved in this computer's credential store (Windows Credential Manager or the system keyring).
words.fileEncrypted: Keys are saved encrypted in {file}, readable only by your user account.
words.filePlain: Keys are saved in {file} without encryption. Only your user account can read the file, but the keys in it are plain text.
words.memory: Keys are kept in memory only and are lost when the daemon restarts.
words.fileUnknown: Keys are saved in {file}, readable only by your user account. The file is encrypted only when PLUGHIVE_SECRETS_PASSPHRASE is set.
words.daemon: Keys are saved by the daemon.
words.daemonBackend: Keys are saved by the daemon ({backend}).

storage.memoryAlertTitle: Keys you add now will not survive a restart

memoryNote.beforeKeychain: This daemon keeps keys in memory only. To keep them, restart it with
memoryNote.afterFile: . With the file option, also set

storage.plainAlertTitle: Keys are saved in a file that is not encrypted

plainNote.afterWords: Anything that can read your files, such as a backup or another program running as you, can read them. On a Mac, restart with
plainNote.afterKeychain: ; on Windows or a Linux desktop,
plainNote.afterPassphrase: set. The daemon does not reuse a plain file once a passphrase is set, so move the old file away and add the keys again.

storage.savedKeyNeverShown: A saved key is never shown again.

library.read: Reads the files it made in the library
library.readAll: Reads every file in the library
library.write: Saves new files to the library
library.full: Reads, saves and removes files in the library

permissions.local: Connects to services on this computer or network: {list}
permissions.localMore: Connects to services on this computer or network: {list} and {count} more
permissions.spawnMore: Runs programs on this computer: {list} and {count} more
permissions.userHome: Programs it runs can read and write your home folder
permissions.llm: Asks a language model through the daemon
permissions.none: No network, programs or files: it works on what you pass it
